scope: Complete recursive Chapter4 Gauduchon reader revision
mathematical_change: Replace an overstrong fixed-flow Gauduchon equivalence in the entropy opening by the correct sufficient statement and all-target initial criterion; add the explicit stationary-flow distinction. Theorem statements and proof bodies remain unchanged.
analytic_review_groups: Gauduchon's scalar elliptic operator has index zero and constant kernel; the adjoint generator has nonzero integral, one sign and strict positivity by Fredholm and the maximum principle.
The full distributional trace mass includes polar mass and controls coefficient measures; it does not bound the nonlinear Monge–Ampère mass. The density inequality keeps its 1/n normalization.
The positive (n-1,n-1) root is smooth through repeated eigenvalues. Hahn–Banach positive extension and a scalar elliptic right inverse reconstruct Lamari's potential for a nonclosed background.
The threshold has a potential minimizer and is positive exactly for a big background. Smooth test attainment requires theta-kappa omega to be a smooth complex Hessian.
Normalized smooth-test closure is compact, convex and metrizable; separation gives its exact polar criterion. All normalized positive Gauduchon currents need not belong to this closure.
Threshold concavity, homogeneity, one-Lipschitz background control and weak minimizing-current stability follow from the fixed linear trace normalization.
Line curvature is minus dd^c log k and has metric-independent Gauduchon degree; scalar trace solvability normalizes curvature without requiring exterior closedness of the test form.

The fiber triangle inequality gives the 2N derivative and 10 epsilon N axis bounds. Phase-invariant averages retain the signed curvature identity and uniform coefficient-adjoint control under C4 Dolbeault perturbations.

Compact sheaf gluing preserves strict margins; convolution by holomorphic linear shears preserves plurisubharmonicity and local real convexity. Homogeneity produces global fiber norms, and weak input needs a separate strict homogeneous function.

The lines convention for projectivization and the tautological dual retain the curvature sign and Levi Schur complement. An ample dual supplies a strict homogeneous function, without asserting real convexity of that function.

Kobayashi curvature uses the horizontal Schur complement; holomorphic osculating sections prove polar plurisubharmonicity. The exact Legendre formula proves uniform strong polar convexity without convexity of the primal square or uniqueness of its maximizer.

Hirzebruch ruling cohomology, canonical class, intersection numbers and the quotient Chern classes are consistent. The incidence argument excludes common fiber curves uniformly over the whole projective parameter space.

Prioritary Hom vanishing retains its Serre-duality twist. Nonsplit extensions are stable, locally free and nonample; the e=0 equality case uses injective Kunneth multiplication. Nilpotent Dolbeault deformations converge in every smooth norm.

Flat-family local freeness, ampleness and stability are open in their stated families. The full prioritary-stack irreducibility theorem is an explicitly retained classical input, without an added semistability hypothesis.

A local curvature failure gives a nondegenerate critical hypersurface test. C2 stability, a countable cover, dilations and summable Oka–Weil approximation choose one Stein hypersurface before choosing the metric.

Concave neighborhood support points yield local holomorphic support and a plurisubharmonic dual norm. Uniform supporting balls give strong real convexity; ample strict input permits smooth replacement.
Closed-submanifold restriction gives the stated least-convexity lower bound. Reciprocal norms give n+r-s upper bounds with one positive radial and r-1 negative vertical directions.

Stable-bundle Hermitian–Einstein existence retains its classical Li–Yau scope. Positive mean curvature and external tensor blocks supply directional positivity with the correct unscaled curvature normalization.

Positive homogeneous plurisubharmonic functions give the sharp total-dimension convexity index. Hopf automorphy, Gauduchon degree and flat restrictions retain their signs and distinguish de Rham triviality from Bott–Chern degree.

A positive pluriharmonic current supported on a smooth hypersurface descends coefficientwise; the top-degree exception is explicit. Smooth Kähler pullback bounds and continuous-coefficient heat regularization do not define arbitrary singular pullbacks.

Zero vertical trace removes mixed coefficients and the remaining nonnegative fiber-harmonic coefficients descend for entire affine or compact curve fibers. The disk counterexample keeps that hypothesis essential.

Adjoint compatibility has codimension one. Constant multipliers characterize the Gauduchon condition; persistence under every potential is equivalent to mass invariance, whereas the normalized energy one-form still needs exterior closedness.

The entropy identity retains the signed torsion and negative gradient terms. Along a fixed stationary target all entropies may be constant on a non-Gauduchon background; the converse criterion quantifies over every initial smooth positive target.

The two-torus Haar averages and determinant derivative give positive initial total-variation growth for K>3, even when both individual entropies initially decrease. The computation assumes initial velocities, not an existence theorem for the flow.
Uniformly bounded capacity convergence extends the persistent adjoint probability; general weak multiplier limits and sequence independence remain open.

Directional RC positivity retains its for-each-vector quantifier and the nonnegative mean-curvature hypothesis. A Gauduchon Poisson equation globalizes positivity; determinant flatness obstructs positive mean or uniform RC positivity.

On a Ricci-flat Kähler surface, directional positivity is equivalent to invertibility of the anti-self-dual curvature block. The retained Derdzinski normalization gives the Bochner identity; parallel distinct eigenlines force flatness in the determinant-zero case.

The integrated sectional-curvature identity retains its Gaussian fourth moments, exact-form term and torsion cancellation against a Kähler reference. On tori, periodic integration forces every metric coefficient to be constant; finite unramified cover descent is legitimate.

Projective first-jet tests use arbitrary Hermitian coefficient matrices. Caratheodory gives finite atomic failure at one level; this differs from a positive matrix-valued measure annihilating all smooth metrics.

Normalized projectors have C2 polynomial density; global-generation right inverses are frame invariant and nested twists need no multiplication surjectivity. Weak probability limits yield the stated all-metric adjoint alternative.

The branched double-cover section decomposition, positive root metric and exact first successful weighted level retain branch-point first-jet vanishing. Fixed very-ample twists nest in steps q, and the example gives no bound on their first successful level.
